methods: Finite-element analysis (PARIS) · rehabilitation design · steel / concrete · drawings

approach: Developed structural models, examined the existing bridge configuration and designed rehabilitation interventions. Prepared calculation and drawing documentation.
outcome: Graduate qualification work defended with Excellent (A). The bridge also serves as a case study in lifecycle-management research.

title: Road Bridge Superstructure with an Orthotropic Deck / Design & Analysis
discipline: Steel bridge design · orthotropic deck · finite-element analysis
summary: Three bridge superstructure schemes were compared; the selected steel bridge uses four main I-girders and an orthotropic deck, with a 473.57 m total length and a (42.30 + 6 × 63.00 + 42.30 m) span arrangement.
role: Individual academic course project — bridge superstructure design and structural analysis.
methods: SOFiSTiK Structural Desktop / SOFiPLUS-X / ASE / MAXIMA / Eigenvalues / TEDDY · Microsoft Excel · BridgeInfluenceAreas · finite-element modelling · staged launching analysis.
challenge: Develop three alternative superstructure schemes for a road bridge with a 420 m navigable opening and two 60 × 10 m navigation clearances; select and develop one configuration for detailed design.
approach: Developed three schemes: a four-I-girder steel superstructure, a twin steel-box-girder alternative with reinforced-concrete approach spans, and a combined box-girder/arch scheme. Variant 1 was selected as the most economically advantageous. The selected scheme was developed through checks of the orthotropic deck, main girders, fatigue, serviceability, local stability, connections, bearings and expansion joints. Beam-grillage and shell finite-element models were built in SOFiSTiK; moving-load positioning and load processing used BridgeInfluenceAreas and Microsoft Excel. A separate construction-stage model examined longitudinal launching and natural vibration.
outcome: Variant 1 was selected as the most economically advantageous. The reported main-girder and orthotropic-deck strength and stability checks satisfy their stated resistance criteria. The separate launching analysis identifies a temporary-support requirement in span No. 7 and a first-mode period exceeding the stated limit at one launching position.

title: Excavation / PLAXIS Analysis
summary: PLAXIS 2D finite-element analysis of a sheet-pile-supported excavation, including staged construction, soil–structure interaction and the assessment of adjacent-building settlements.
role: Individual academic project — geotechnical modelling and excavation-support design.
methods: PLAXIS 2D · finite-element modelling · soil–structure interaction · staged excavation · pore-pressure analysis
challenge: Assess the behaviour of a sheet-pile-supported excavation in a built-up environment, accounting for the construction sequence, pore-pressure response and effects on neighbouring foundations.
approach: Developed a two-dimensional finite-element model in PLAXIS 2D using the engineering-geological profile and selected support layout. Analysed the excavation in construction stages, including installation of the sheet-pile wall and struts, sequential excavation, pore-pressure response, and deformation of the surrounding soil and nearby foundations. Selected the sheet-pile and strut sections through iterative checks.
outcome: Selected Larsen AZ 38 sheet piles and welded steel pipe struts Ø820 × 16 mm. The reported maximum sheet-pile bending moment is 602.2 kN·m, with a verification ratio of 0.4686 (<1.0).
image_alt: Selected PLAXIS 2D finite-element analysis illustrations for a sheet-pile-supported excavation.
calculation_software: PLAXIS 2D — finite-element modelling of soil–structure interaction.
calculation_summary: The model evaluates the excavation in staged construction, including ground response, pore-pressure changes and the effect on adjacent foundations. Reported vertical displacements at the assessment points are −28.85, −28.78 and −27.26 mm. The maximum sheet-pile bending moment is 602.2 kN·m, with a reported verification ratio of 0.4686 (<1.0).

title: Urban Pedestrian Tunnel / Shallow Cut-and-Cover Design
discipline: Underground structures · urban transport · reinforced concrete · finite-element analysis
summary: Academic design of a shallow pedestrian underpass in Saint Petersburg, from pedestrian-flow observations and three layout alternatives to structural analysis and construction planning.
role: Individual academic design project — site investigation, alternative development, structural modelling, calculation documentation and construction planning.
methods: Pedestrian-flow survey · comparative design · SOFiSTiK / SOFiPLUS-X / SSD / Report Browser · Winkler foundation model · reinforced-concrete design · cut-and-cover construction
challenge: Design a grade-separated pedestrian connection at the Savushkina Street / Lipovaya Alley intersection near Staraya Derevnya transport interchange, addressing pedestrian–vehicle conflicts, accessibility and future pedestrian demand.
approach: Undertook short-duration pedestrian counts, estimated design demand, developed three H-shaped alternatives, compared the reported construction quantities, modelled the selected tunnel lining with a Winkler elastic foundation in SOFiSTiK, and developed detailed sections and a construction sequence.
outcome: Selected Variant 1, a precast reinforced-concrete H-shaped tunnel with a 33.80 m main passage, four passenger lifts and 0.88 m of overburden. The report includes load combinations, internal-force diagrams, sectional checks and a construction scheme. Academic design study; not a constructed project.
